feed.headline: French weekend protests to be limited to union demos only, says Macron
feed.ai: Some cities including Lyon and Nice have banned all protests, and the French president said only authorised demos would be allowed.
feed.frag: Highlights the limits of national coordination

feed.headline: Watch: Will Ukraine get the support needed as tensions with US rise?
feed.ai: Zelensky thanked the "real leaders" ahead of a meeting with the EU in Brussels.

feed.headline: Celebrations in Serbia after veteran ruler Vučić loses election to student-led protest movement
feed.ai: The populist right-wing leader of 12 years says it is "clear" his party has lost the vote billed as a referendum on the country's future.

feed.headline: Joy and disbelief on Serbian streets as Vučić concedes election defeat
feed.ai: BBC correspondent Nick Thorpe reports from Belgrade, where there were rapturous celebrations following the victory of the student-led movement.

feed.headline: Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push
feed.ai: President Vladimir Putin does not feel under pressure right now to end the war, the BBC's Russia Editor writes.

feed.headline: Who actually controls Ukraine's access to Starlink?
feed.ai: President Zelensky says limits to the technology continue to affect Ukrainian forces, while US officials and Elon Musk offer conflicting accounts of who controls it.

feed.headline: Are the French riots a warning of an intense election to come?
feed.ai: Rioting, looting and vandalism has gripped France over the weekend after protests spiralled out of control across the country.

feed.headline: Norway Pushes Back After Trump Disparages It Over Nobel Prize Decision
feed.ai: Norwegian officials emphasized that their country does not have any influence over who receives the Peace Prize, after President Trump used crude language to express his frustration.

feed.headline: Trump officials back Orbán bid for UN secretary-general, WSJ reports
feed.ai: The WSJ reports that Trump administration officials are floating former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán for UN secretary-general, potentially backed by the US, Russia and China, though nothing is confirmed and his selection remains uncertain.

feed.headline: Serbia: crowds celebrate in Belgrade after Vučić admits defeat
feed.ai: Crowds celebrated in Belgrade after President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat for his ruling party in Serbia's snap parliamentary election, following nearly two years of student-led demonstrations.

feed.headline: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
feed.ai: The Student List has emerged from almost two years of anti-corruption protests to form the biggest challenge to Vučić's rule.

feed.headline: Why a student protest movement is challenging 12 years of Vučić rule in Serbia
feed.ai: After two years of student protests, Serbians vote on Sunday in elections that could bring down the ruling party.
